questions: Should the plot be displayed (plt.show()) or just prepared (e.g., plt.plot calls) without showing, or should it be saved to a file?
Are the real and imaginary parts plotted against the same x-values (the input array), or is the x-axis something else like indices?
Should the function add labels, legend, grid, or title to the plot, or is a minimal plot sufficient?
Is the complex distribution defined as real_part + 1j*imag_part (as in reference) or some other combination like abs(real_part) + 1j*abs(imag_part)?
Does 'combining their absolute values' in the prompt refer to the plot (clarification says not) or to the complex distribution creation?
Should the function close the plot after showing or leave it open for further modifications?
What should happen if x contains NaN or inf values? Should the function handle them or propagate through norm.pdf?
Is the plot required to be generated every time, or only if a certain condition is met (e.g., non-empty x)?
